name: The Right to Disconnect: Can You Refuse Augmentation?
author: GLMZ Civil Liberties Union
body:
The question is no longer 'can you get augmented?' The question is 'can you refuse?'

In theory, yes. No GLMZ jurisdiction mandates cybernetic augmentation. The Gradient Compact's Article 3 protects individual bodily autonomy. You cannot be forced to receive an implant.

In practice, the economic and social pressure to augment is so pervasive that refusal carries consequences indistinguishable from formal prohibition:

— EMPLOYMENT: 73% of Tier 3+ jobs require augmentation. An unaugmented worker is locked out of three-quarters of the middle-class job market. — INSURANCE: Health insurance premiums for unaugmented individuals are 40% higher than for augmented ones, because augmented individuals have better health monitoring and faster emergency response through their implants. — SOCIAL: Dating platforms report that 68% of users filter out unaugmented matches. Social networks optimized for BCI interaction are inaccessible to the unaugmented. — SAFETY: In districts with high crime rates, personal defense augmentation (reinforced skeleton, enhanced reflexes, subdermal armor) is not a luxury. It is survival.

The right to refuse augmentation exists on paper. The world has been reorganized to make that right economically, socially, and physically untenable.

This is coercion by architecture. Nobody forces you to get chrome. The world simply becomes unlivable without it. The Saint is not mandatory. It is merely necessary.
